Prominent Biden administration alumni are winning in a handful of notable races, with Keisha Lance Bottoms — the one-time Atlanta mayor turned Biden’s senior adviser and director of the Office of Public Engagement — leading the pack by flipping Georgia’s governorship.

articles.title: Mamdani Ballot Proposals on Public Space, Street Safety and More Pass in NYC
articles.summary: In a sweep, all five proposals on the back of New Yorkers’ ballots passed by a large margin Tuesday evening, giving a boost to Mayor Zohran Mamdani in his first year in office. With nearly all precincts reporting, each ballot proposal received at least 61% of the vote.

articles.title: Kathy Hochul Sails to Re-Election Amid Democratic Blue Wave
articles.summary: Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul locked down a second full term as the leader of New York State with a defeat of Republican Bruce Blakeman, the challenger backed by President Donald Trump, in a contest centered on affordability.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed Wins Senate Seat With Pro-Palestine Campaign
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed defeated Mike Rogers in the U.S. Senate race in Michigan early Wednesday, outlasting months of Islamophobic vitriol and offering a bright spot to progressives looking to test their message ahead of the 2028 presidential primary. El-Sayed will be the first-ever Muslim U.S. senator.

articles.summary: The hard-to-beat Maine Republican was defeated by a progressive new to the national scene as Democrats took the Senate.

articles.title: Republicans underperform as first midterm votes are counted
articles.summary: The first midterm votes counted on Tuesday night suggest a tough night for Republicans, in line with polling that has put Democrats well ahead in the battle for Congress on the strength of public frustration with President Donald Trump’s agenda. In Indiana and Kentucky, where most polls closed at 6 pm ET, Democrats ran well ahead of their early vote totals two years ago.
